content:
alex_sales: Hey team, PulseCare's security team returned a questionnaire. Key asks: Private deployment, preserve original client IP for their WAF/rate-limits, provide a stable outbound IP for allowlisting, and confirm whether TLS inspection is feasible. They also want a rough monthly delta vs Hosted. Can we sketch options and a quick firewall snippet they can give to infra?

tara_neteng: TL;DR options: VPC peering/transit preserves client src IP end-to-end; PrivateLink (interface endpoint) does not preserve src IP (traffic appears from endpoint ENI). To get a single stable egress IP you need NAT/EIP in the path (Transit/VPC NAT).

ben_se: Quick patterns we propose:
- Pattern A: VPC peering/transit -> our Private deployment in their account (or cross-account peering). Client IP preserved. Requires route propagation, shared route tables, and security review.
- Pattern B: PrivateLink endpoint + a small L4 proxy in customer VPC that forwards X-Forwarded-For. Works when app trusts header.
- Pattern C: Private deployment with dedicated egress NAT in transit account (we can map a single EIP back to them). Good for strict allowlist needs but breaks original src IP unless combined with conntrack mapping.

maya_compliance: On TLS inspection: important to ask whether they need transparent inspection (MITM) or can accept termination at a trusted proxy. If their apps do cert pinning, MITM will fail. Also ask about regulated-data rules for key custody.

alex_sales: Can you paste a minimal firewall ACL we can send? And a POC-level monthly delta (ballpark) comparing Hosted -> Dedicated/Private with static egress? They need numbers for SOW draft.

tara_neteng: Firewall example (replace prefixes/EIP):
```
# Allow egress from customer app subnets to Redwood Private (example)
ALLOW OUT TCP 443 FROM 10.10.0.0/22 TO 203.0.113.128/26
# If using NAT/EIP for single outbound IP
NAT 10.10.0.0/22 -> 34.200.77.88
# If using PrivateLink, allow ENI ranges per-AZ (we supply ENI list pre-handoff)
```

tara_neteng: Routing notes: with peering you need to ensure no overlapping CIDRs; Transit GW approach scales better for multi-vpc. Also we need an expected sessions/conntrack limit if using NAT.

ben_se: Ballpark monthly POC deltas (very rough):
- Hosted API: $0 setup, pay-as-you-go tokens. No static egress guarantee.
- Dedicated reserved (POC tier): approx $6k-$18k/month depending on GPU tier & reserved qps.
- Private deployment (customer-managed infra) baseline: infra cost + our license, typically $12k-$40k/month on POC depending on sizing.
- Private + managed static egress (single EIP managed by us): additional $800-$2,000/month + per-GB egress charge.
These are placeholders; exact quote from Sales Ops.

maya_compliance: Security answers to the questionnaire:
- KMS: customer-managed KMS supported for Private (we support AWS KMS and external key-wrap options).
- Audit: request traces and metadata can be exported; retention options 30/90/365 days.
- TLS inspection: note the compatibility caveat (cert pinning). Recommend a dedicated proxy model if inspection is mandatory.

alex_sales: Great. Can someone volunteer to join a handoff call with PulseCare's infra team tomorrow 11am PT? We'll go through CIDRs and finalize the NAT EIP plan.

tara_neteng: I can take it. I'll bring a route table example and NAT sizing guidance.

ben_se: I'll attend to discuss header propagation and app changes for X-Forwarded-For.

maya_compliance: I'll join for the questionnaire signoff and KMS notes.

ops-bot: Meeting scheduled: PulseCare-network-handoff on 2025-06-13 11:00 PT. Link: https://meet.redwood.example/pulsecare-1778888123

alex_sales: Thanks all 44d I'll send the invite to PulseCare and attach the ACL snippet + our draft security responses. Action items: Tara to send route table + NAT sizing; Ben to write short guidance on trusting X-Forwarded-For and header injection risks; Maya to produce the TLS inspection compatibility blurb.
